Below, we’ll dive into how you can customize a generic invoice to be unique to your business. The first time you create an invoice, you'll need to add some information to the blank invoice template. Add your company details in the From section, including the name, phone number, and address Fill out your client’s details in the For section, including name, email, and address Add each line item, along with a description, rate, and quantity If applicable, enter the tax rate, type of currency, and discount amount Write payment instructions and terms in Notes section Customize your invoice by adding a logo and selecting your brand color How to send an invoice Once your first invoice is complete, you’ll need to learn how to send it to your client. Our invoice generator gives you two easy options to send an invoice. First, compose an email to your client. You can include a link to your invoice in the email or send them a PDF of the invoice as an attachment. The client simply clicks on the link or the attachment to see the invoice. Then, check in on the status of your sent invoice. If you email your invoice directly from Invoice Simple, you will receive a notification when your customer views the invoice. The notification is useful for following up with clients to confirm payment. Essential elements of an invoice There are 9 main elements of an invoice. Some of these elements are necessary, while others are extra or used only for customization. Header Headers should clearly state the purpose of a document. Our software allows you to generate estimates, invoices, and receipts. Including a header allows you and the client to tell them apart quickly. This will save you time when reviewing your records or completing taxes. Note the image marked “Company Logo” to the right of the header. Here, you can add in your own logo for more professional estimates, invoices, and receipts. If your business does not have a logo, you can leave this section blank as long as the rest of the invoice is laid out properly. Company name and details When creating an invoice, you should include the legal name and contact details of your business. This should include your address, phone number, and email address. Usually, company information is written near the top of the invoice to create a clear differentiation between the company providing the goods or services and the company receiving them. Name and Details of Client Clearly state the name and contact details of your client. These contact details should include an address, phone number, and email address. Invoice Number Each invoice has a unique identifier called an invoice number. Invoice numbers can help keep track of multiple invoices. Invoice numbers can be formatted in various ways. These formats can include file numbers (INV0001), unique billing codes, or date-based purchase order numbers. If you use Invoice Simple invoicing software to automatically manage your invoice number, the software will create a unique invoice number for each document. If you wish to use your own custom format for your invoice number, you can update each invoice number yourself each time you use the invoice generator. Date It’s important to include the date that each invoice is issued. This can clear up confusion when the same customer receives multiple invoices. Because payment is usually due a specified number of days after receipt of the invoice, including the date is an important part of showing when payment is due. Description of Goods or Services Rendered In box six, you should include separate line items for each good or service you are providing. Each row should include the following: Name of the goods or service provided. Unit price or hourly rate. Quantity or number of hours worked. Itemized fees Next, add any tax, shipping and handling, or extra fees that apply to the goods or services provided. We recommend listing these taxes and fees as separate line items, as some companies use different internal budgets to cover these fees. Balance Due The invoice generator will calculate the total balance due from the line items you entered in boxes six and seven. Terms, Conditions and Payment Instructions The terms and conditions of payment on an invoice is the part most frequently overlooked. The standard payment terms can vary by industry, your company’s policy, or previous history with the customer. It’s important to clearly state the consequences of either party breaking this agreement. These penalties can include late fees or additional charges. You can also add your preferred payment method here, whether it’s cheque, cash, bank transfer, PayPal, or credit card. Then, add in the payment instructions. For example, write your account number

sources.title: 5 Best Automated Invoice Reminder Tools for Freelancers in 2026 (Including Free Options) | Landolio
sources.excerpt: Landolio Tools Guides Free Checklist Landolio Free Tools Blog Home → Blog → Invoice Reminder Tools 5 Best Automated Invoice Reminder Tools for Freelancers in 2026 (Including Free Options) Published 19 February 2026 · 9 min read Late payments are the silent killer of freelance businesses. According to a 2025 IPSE survey, 71% of UK freelancers have experienced late payment at least once, with the average overdue invoice sitting unpaid for 23 days past its due date. That's nearly a month of working capital stuck in someone else's bank account. The solution? An automated invoice reminder tool for freelancers — software that chases your unpaid invoices so you don't have to. No more awkward "just checking in" emails. No more forgotten follow-ups. Just consistent, professional reminders that land in your client's inbox on schedule. We've tested and compared the five best options available in 2026. Whether you're a solo designer billing three clients or a consultancy managing dozens, there's a tool here for you. TL;DR: If you want a free, purpose-built automated invoice reminder tool for freelancers, Landolio is the best starting point. For full-suite accounting, FreshBooks or Xero are worth the investment. What to Look for in an Invoice Reminder Tool Before diving into the reviews, here's what actually matters when choosing an automated invoice reminder tool for freelancers: Customisable reminder sequences — pre-due, on-due, and overdue cadences you can tailor (like the 5-email late payment sequence we recommend) Tone control — friendly vs. firm language depending on how late the payment is Client tracking — dashboard showing who owes what and when Ease of setup — you should be sending reminders within minutes, not hours Pricing that makes sense — the tool should cost less than the payments it recovers The 5 Best Automated Invoice Reminder Tools for Freelancers 1. Landolio — Best Free Option for Payment Follow-Ups Free tier available · Pro from £9/mo Landolio is a dedicated invoice follow-up tool built specifically for freelancers and small agencies. Unlike the all-in-one accounting platforms on this list, Landolio does one thing and does it exceptionally well: it automates your payment reminders with intelligent, multi-step sequences. The free tier supports up to 3 active clients with automated email reminders, making it genuinely usable without paying a penny. The Pro plan (£9/month) unlocks unlimited clients, custom reminder templates, escalation sequences, and analytics showing which reminders actually get opened. What sets Landolio apart is its focus. There's no bloated invoicing suite to navigate — you add your invoices, set your reminder rules, and the system handles the rest. It's the kind of tool you set up once on a Sunday afternoon and then forget about, until the money starts landing faster. FreshBooks — Best All-in-One for Invoice Management From £12/mo (Lite plan) FreshBooks has been a freelancer favourite for over a decade, and for good reason. Its invoicing features are polished, intuitive, and deeply integrated with time tracking, expense management, and basic accounting. Automated payment reminders are built into every plan. You can configure reminders to go out at set intervals — before the due date, on the day, and at custom intervals after. The emails are professional and customisable, and you can track when clients open them. The catch? You're paying for an entire accounting suite even if you only need reminders. The Lite plan starts at £12/month and caps you at 5 billable clients. If you need more, the Plus plan jumps to £22/month. Xero — Best for UK Freelancers Who Need Accounting From £16/mo (Starter plan) Xero is the go-to accounting platform for UK freelancers and small businesses, particularly those who work with an accountant. Its invoice reminder feature lets you set up to three automatic reminders per invoice — before, on, and after the due date. The platform's real strength lies in its accounting depth: bank reconciliation, VAT returns, multi-currency support, and a massive app marketplace. If you're already using Xero for your books, turning on automated reminders is a no-brainer. However, Xero's reminder feature is somewhat basic compared to dedicated tools. You get limited template customisation, no escalation logic, and no analytics on whether clients actually read the reminders. It also supports late fees — automatically adding a percentage or flat fee to overdue invoices, which can be a powerful motivator for slow-paying clients. The trade-off is polish. report.problem: Freelance designers may spend significant time manually following up on unpaid invoices, impacting their productivity and cash flow.
uncertainties: The exact amount of time freelance designers spend on invoice follow-up.
The specific features most valued by freelance designers in an invoice follow-up tool.

report.mvp: A simple tool that allows freelance designers to input client and invoice details, set up automated reminder schedules (e.g., pre-due, on-due, overdue), and send these reminders via email. The tool should have a free tier for a limited number of clients.
report.nextExperiment: Develop a basic prototype of the automated invoice reminder tool and recruit 10-15 freelance designers to test its usability and effectiveness in reducing follow-up time and improving payment speed. Gather feedback on desired features and willingness to pay for advanced functionalities.
report.reason: The evidence strongly suggests that late payments are a common pain point for freelancers, and automated reminder tools are a viable solution. Several tools exist, but there's an opportunity for a focused, potentially free or low-cost solution specifically for freelance designers.

validationPlan.audience: Freelance graphic designers, web designers, and other creative freelancers.
validationPlan.offer: A free, easy-to-use automated invoice reminder tool for a limited number of clients, with an option to upgrade for more features.
validationPlan.channel: Online design communities, freelance platforms (e.g., Upwork, Fiverr), social media groups for designers.
validationPlan.successMetric: At least 50 freelance designers sign up for the prototype, and 70% of active users report a reduction in time spent on invoice follow-up or an improvement in payment times.
validationPlan.stopMetric: Fewer than 20 freelance designers sign up for the prototype within the first month, or less than 50% of active users engage with the reminder feature.
